```{r setup, echo = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 7, fig.align = "center")
```

```{r packages-and-settings}
options(bitmapType = "cairo")
library(tximport)
library(rtracklayer)
library(DESeq2)
library(tidyverse)
library(reactable)
library(plotly)
library(RUVSeq)
library(edgeR)
disease_colors <- c("control" = "#0072B2", "T2D case" = "#D55E00")
timepoint_colors <- c("baseline" = "#009E73", "follow-up" = "#CC79A7")
outlier_colors <- c("No" = "#7A7A7A", "Potential" = "#E69F00", "Unambiguous" = "#D55E00")
outlier_binary_colors <- c("No" = "#7A7A7A", "Flagged" = "#D55E00")
timepoint_shapes <- c("baseline" = 19, "follow-up" = 21)
outlier_shapes <- c("No" = 16, "Potential" = 17, "Unambiguous" = 15)
cchc_theme <- function() {
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "top",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )}
theme_set(cchc_theme())
format_plotly <- function(p){
  p |>
    layout(
      hovermode = "closest",
      font = list(size = 12),
      margin = list(l = 70, r = 40, b = 60, t = 40)
    ) |>
    config(displaylogo = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)}
qc <- read_tsv("../output/qc/sample_qc_summary.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(
    library_size_input_million = salmon_processed_fragments / 1e6,
    library_size_output_million = salmon_mapped_fragments / 1e6,
    rrna_mean_pct = (rrna_r1_pct + rrna_r2_pct) / 2,
    hbrna_mean_pct = (hbrna_r1_pct + hbrna_r2_pct) / 2
  )
```

# Data Summary

This section summarises the samples included in this analysis, including the number of individuals, longitudinal timepoints, and disease groups. Each individual contributes paired baseline and follow-up samples.

```{r data-summary}
tibble(
  Metric = c("Samples", "Individuals", "Baseline samples", "Follow-up samples"),
  Value = c(nrow(qc), n_distinct(qc$individual), sum(qc$timepoint == "baseline"), sum(qc$timepoint == "follow-up"))
) |>
  reactable(pagination = FALSE, bordered = TRUE, striped = TRUE, highlight = TRUE)
```

The table below shows the distribution of samples across disease state and timepoint.

```{r group-summary}
qc |>
  dplyr::count(disease_state, timepoint, name = "Samples") |>
  reactable(pagination = FALSE, bordered = TRUE, striped = TRUE, highlight = TRUE)
```

## Sample QC Table

This table combines the main sample-level QC metrics used throughout the report. It includes library size, mapping performance, library compatibility, fragment characteristics, and whole-blood RNA composition.

```{r sample-qc-table}
sample_qc <- qc |>
  transmute(
    run, sample, individual, disease_state, timepoint,
    library_size_input_million = round(library_size_input_million, 2),
    library_size_output_million = round(library_size_output_million, 2),
    mapping_rate = round(mapping_rate, 2),
    library_type,
    library_compatible_pct = round(library_compatible_pct, 2),
    decoy_pct = round(decoy_pct, 2),
    fragment_length_mean = round(fragment_length_mean, 2),
    fragment_length_sd = round(fragment_length_sd, 2),
    rrna_mean_pct = round(rrna_mean_pct, 2),
    hbrna_mean_pct = round(hbrna_mean_pct, 2)
  )
reactable(
  sample_qc,
  searchable = TRUE, sortable = TRUE, resizable = TRUE, filterable = TRUE,
  showPageSizeOptions = TRUE, defaultPageSize = 10, striped = TRUE, highlight = TRUE,
  columns = list(
    run = colDef(name = "Run"),
    sample = colDef(name = "Sample"),
    individual = colDef(name = "Individual"),
    disease_state = colDef(name = "Disease state"),
    timepoint = colDef(name = "Timepoint"),
    library_size_input_million = colDef(name = "Input (M fragments)"),
    library_size_output_million = colDef(name = "Mapped (M fragments)"),
    mapping_rate = colDef(name = "Mapping (%)"),
    library_type = colDef(name = "Library type"),
    library_compatible_pct = colDef(name = "Compatible (%)"),
    decoy_pct = colDef(name = "Decoy (%)"),
    fragment_length_mean = colDef(name = "Fragment mean"),
    fragment_length_sd = colDef(name = "Fragment SD"),
    rrna_mean_pct = colDef(name = "rRNA (%)"),
    hbrna_mean_pct = colDef(name = "HbRNA (%)")
  ))
```

## Salmon Library Type

This table summarises the Salmon-inferred library type across all samples. Consistent library-type inference helps confirm that the sequencing libraries show similar strand-orientation characteristics across the dataset.

```{r library-type}
qc |>
  dplyr::count(library_type, name = "Samples") |>
  reactable(
    pagination = FALSE, bordered = TRUE, striped = TRUE, highlight = TRUE,
    columns = list(library_type = colDef(name = "Library type"))
  )
```

# Salmon QC {.tabset}

This section reviews sample-level technical metrics derived from Salmon quantification.

## Mapping Rate

Mapping rate represents the proportion of processed fragments successfully mapped during Salmon quantification. Samples with relatively low mapping rates are reviewed together with library size, library compatibility, decoy alignment, and RNA composition.

```{r mapping-rate}
p <- qc |>
  arrange(mapping_rate) |>
  mutate(
    sample_order = row_number(),
    hover = paste0(
      "Run: ", run, "<br>Individual: ", individual, "<br>Group: ", disease_state,
      "<br>Timepoint: ", timepoint, "<br>Mapping rate: ", round(mapping_rate, 2), "%"
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = sample_order, y = mapping_rate, color = timepoint, text = hover)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = timepoint_colors) +
  labs(x = "Samples ordered by mapping rate", y = "Salmon mapping rate (%)", color = "Timepoint")
format_plotly(ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text"))
```

## Library Size

Library size was examined at two stages. Input library size represents the number of fragments processed by Salmon, while output library size represents the number of fragments successfully mapped. Comparing these values helps identify samples with unusually low sequencing depth or substantial loss of fragments during mapping.

```{r library-size}
library_size_plot <- qc |>
  arrange(library_size_input_million) |>
  mutate(sample_order = row_number()) |>
  dplyr::select(
    run, individual, disease_state, timepoint, sample_order, library_size_input_million,
    library_size_output_million
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(library_size_input_million, library_size_output_million), names_to = "library_stage",
    values_to = "library_size_million"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    library_stage = recode(library_stage, library_size_input_million = "Input", library_size_output_million = "Output"),
    hover = paste0(
      "Run: ", run, "<br>Individual: ", individual, "<br>Group: ", disease_state, "<br>Timepoint: ", timepoint,
      "<br>Stage: ", library_stage, "<br>Library size: ", round(library_size_million, 2), " million fragments"
    ))
p <- library_size_plot |>
  ggplot(aes(x = sample_order, y = library_size_million, color = timepoint, text = hover)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = timepoint_colors) +
  facet_wrap(~ library_stage, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Samples ordered by input library size", y = "Library size (million fragments)", color = "Timepoint")
format_plotly(ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text"))
```

### Input vs Output

```{r library-size-input-output}
p <- qc |>
  mutate(
    hover = paste0(
      "Run: ", run, "<br>Individual: ", individual, "<br>Group: ", disease_state, "<br>Timepoint: ", timepoint,
      "<br>Input: ", round(library_size_input_million, 2), " M",
      "<br>Output: ", round(library_size_output_million, 2), " M",
      "<br>Mapping: ", round(mapping_rate, 2), "%"
    )) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = library_size_input_million, y = library_size_output_million, color = disease_state,
    shape = timepoint, text = hover
  )) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = disease_colors) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = timepoint_shapes) +
  labs(
    x = "Input library size (million processed fragments)",
    y = "Output library size (million mapped fragments)",
    color = "Disease state",
    shape = "Timepoint")
format_plotly(ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text"))
```

## Library Compatibility

Library compatibility represents the proportion of mapped fragments that are consistent with the inferred library type. Samples with relatively low compatibility may indicate differences in library structure or mapping behaviour and are therefore reviewed together with mapping rate, decoy alignment, and other QC metrics.

```{r library-compatibility}
p <- qc |>
  arrange(library_compatible_pct) |>
  mutate(
    sample_order = row_number(),
    hover = paste0(
      "Run: ", run, "<br>Individual: ", individual, "<br>Group: ", disease_state,
      "<br>Timepoint: ", timepoint, "<br>Compatible: ", round(library_compatible_pct, 2), "%"
    )) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = sample_order, y = library_compatible_pct, color = timepoint, text = hover)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = timepoint_colors) +
  labs(x = "Samples ordered by compatibility", y = "Library-compatible fragments (%)", color = "Timepoint")
format_plotly(ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text"))
```

## Decoy Alignment

Decoy alignment represents the proportion of processed fragments that preferentially align to decoy sequences rather than the annotated transcriptome. Elevated decoy proportions may indicate increased off-target or ambiguous alignment and are therefore interpreted together with mapping rate, library compatibility, and other technical QC metrics.

```{r decoy-alignment}
p <- qc |>
  arrange(decoy_pct) |>
  mutate(
    sample_order = row_number(),
    hover = paste0(
      "Run: ", run, "<br>Individual: ", individual, "<br>Group: ", disease_state,
      "<br>Timepoint: ", timepoint, "<br>Decoy: ", round(decoy_pct, 2), "%"
    )) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = sample_order, y = decoy_pct, color = timepoint, text = hover)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = timepoint_colors) +
  labs(x = "Samples ordered by decoy proportion", y = "Decoy fragments (%)", color = "Timepoint")
format_plotly(ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text"))
```

## Fragment Length

Fragment length reflects the estimated insert size distribution of each RNA-seq library. Samples with unusually short or long mean fragment lengths may indicate differences in library preparation, RNA integrity, or sequencing characteristics and are therefore reviewed as part of the overall technical QC assessment.

```{r fragment-length}
p <- qc |>
  arrange(fragment_length_mean) |>
  mutate(
    sample_order = row_number(),
    hover = paste0(
      "Run: ", run, "<br>Individual: ", individual, "<br>Group: ", disease_state,
      "<br>Timepoint: ", timepoint,
      "<br>Mean fragment length: ", round(fragment_length_mean, 2), " bp"
    )) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = sample_order, y = fragment_length_mean, color = timepoint, text = hover)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = timepoint_colors) +
  labs(x = "Samples ordered by fragment length", y = "Mean fragment length (bp)", color = "Timepoint")
format_plotly(ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text"))
```

# Whole-blood QC {.tabset}

Whole-blood RNA-seq can contain substantial variation in ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and haemoglobin-derived RNA (HbRNA). These components are examined separately because unusually high proportions may influence global expression patterns and contribute to sample-level variation.

## rRNA

rRNA content was reviewed across samples to identify libraries with unusually high ribosomal RNA proportions. R1 and R2 values were also compared to assess whether elevated rRNA levels were consistent between paired reads.

```{r rrna-samples}
p <- qc |>
  arrange(rrna_mean_pct) |>
  mutate(
    sample_order = row_number(),
    hover = paste0(
      "Run: ", run, "<br>Individual: ", individual, "<br>Group: ", disease_state,
      "<br>Timepoint: ", timepoint, "<br>rRNA: ", round(rrna_mean_pct, 2), "%"
    )) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = sample_order, y = rrna_mean_pct, color = timepoint, text = hover)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = timepoint_colors) +
  labs(x = "Samples ordered by rRNA content", y = "Mean rRNA mapping (%)", color = "Timepoint")
format_plotly(ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text"))
```

```{r rrna-r1-r2}
p <- qc |>
  mutate(hover = paste0(
    "Run: ", run, "<br>Individual: ", individual, "<br>Timepoint: ", timepoint,
    "<br>R1: ", round(rrna_r1_pct, 2), "%", "<br>R2: ", round(rrna_r2_pct, 2), "%"
  )) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = rrna_r1_pct, y = rrna_r2_pct, color = timepoint, text = hover)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = timepoint_colors) +
  labs(x = "rRNA R1 (%)", y = "rRNA R2 (%)", color = "Timepoint")
format_plotly(ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text"))
```

## HbRNA

HbRNA content was examined because haemoglobin-derived transcripts can account for a substantial proportion of whole-blood RNA-seq reads and may influence downstream expression structure. R1 and R2 values were compared to assess the consistency of HbRNA enrichment within each sample.

```{r hbrna-samples}

  ggplot(aes(x = sample_order, y = hbrna_mean_pct, color = timepoint, text = hover)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = timepoint_colors) +
  labs(x = "Samples ordered by HbRNA content", y = "Mean HbRNA mapping (%)", color = "Timepoint")
format_plotly(ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text"))
```

```{r hbrna-r1-r2}
p <- qc |>
  mutate(hover = paste0(

  )) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = hbrna_r1_pct, y = hbrna_r2_pct, color = timepoint, text = hover)) +
```

# QC Summary

This table summarises the observed minimum, median, and maximum values for the main QC metrics across all samples. It provides a cohort-level reference for interpreting individual samples and helps place potentially unusual values in the context of the overall dataset.

```{r qc-summary}
qc_summary <- qc |>
  summarise(
    across(
      c(library_size_input_million, library_size_output_million, mapping_rate, library_compatible_pct, decoy_pct,
        fragment_length_mean, fragment_length_sd, rrna_mean_pct, hbrna_mean_pct),
      list(min = ~ min(.x, na.rm = TRUE), median = ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE), max = ~ max(.x, na.rm = TRUE))
    )) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("metric", ".value"), names_pattern = "(.+)_(min|median|max)$") |>
  mutate(
    across(c(min, median, max), ~ round(.x, 2)),
    metric = metric |> str_replace_all("_", " ") |> str_to_sentence()
  ) |>
  rename(Metric = metric, Minimum = min, Median = median, Maximum = max)
reactable(qc_summary, pagination = FALSE, bordered = TRUE, striped = TRUE, highlight = TRUE)
```

# Expression-level Assessment

## Import Salmon Counts

Gene-level expression counts were imported from Salmon transcript quantification using tximport and the GRCh38 gene annotation. Transcript-level estimates were summarised to genes before downstream expression-level quality assessment.

```{r import-expression}
sample_metadata <- read_csv("../config/PRJNA762935.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::select(run = Run, age = AGE, sex)
sample_info <- read_tsv("../config/samples.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  left_join(sample_metadata, by = "run")
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(sample_metadata$run), all(sample_info$run %in% sample_metadata$run))
quant_files <- file.path("../data/quant", sample_info$run, "quant.sf")
names(quant_files) <- sample_info$run
if (!all(file.exists(quant_files))) {
  stop("Some Salmon quant.sf files are missing.")
}
gtf <- rtracklayer::import("../data/reference/Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.116.gtf.gz")
tx2gene <- as.data.frame(gtf) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(transcript_id), !is.na(gene_id)) |>
  dplyr::select(transcript_id, gene_id) |>
  distinct()
txi <- tximport(quant_files, type = "salmon", tx2gene = tx2gene, ignoreTxVersion = TRUE, dropInfReps = TRUE)
gene_counts <- txi$counts
stopifnot(ncol(gene_counts) == nrow(sample_info), identical(colnames(gene_counts), sample_info$run))
tibble(
  Metric = c("Salmon quant files", "Imported samples", "Genes", "Samples missing age", "Samples missing sex"),
  Value = c(
    length(quant_files), ncol(gene_counts), nrow(gene_counts), sum(is.na(sample_info$age)),
    sum(is.na(sample_info$sex))
  )) |>
  reactable(pagination = FALSE, bordered = TRUE, striped = TRUE, highlight = TRUE)
```

## Variance-stabilised Expression

Low-expression genes were filtered before PCA to reduce noise from genes with minimal information across the dataset. Genes were retained when they had at least 10 counts in at least five samples.
Variance-stabilising transformation (VST) was then applied to the filtered expression matrix. VST reduces the dependence of variance on mean expression and provides a more suitable scale for sample-level PCA and exploratory structure assessment.

```{r vst-expression}
coldata <- as.data.frame(sample_info)
rownames(coldata) <- coldata$run
stopifnot(identical(rownames(coldata), colnames(txi$counts)))
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromTximport(txi = txi, colData = coldata, design = ~ 1)
keep <- rowSums(counts(dds) >= 10) >= 5
dds <- dds[keep, ]
vsd <- vst(dds, blind = TRUE)
vst_matrix <- assay(vsd)
tibble(
  Metric = c("Genes before filtering", "Genes retained for PCA", "Samples"),
  Value = c(nrow(gene_counts), nrow(vst_matrix), ncol(vst_matrix))) |>
  reactable(pagination = FALSE, bordered = TRUE, striped = TRUE, highlight = TRUE)
```

## PCA

Principal component analysis (PCA) was used to examine global sample-level expression structure after variance-stabilising transformation. PCA reduces the high-dimensional gene-expression matrix into a smaller number of orthogonal components that capture the major sources of variation between samples.
The percentage associated with each principal component represents the proportion of total expression variance explained by that component. A lower percentage is not inherently better; the components are used to identify major expression patterns, sample clustering, and potentially unusual samples.

```{r run-pca}
pca <- prcomp(t(vst_matrix), center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)
variance_explained <- (pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2)) * 100
pca_data <- as.data.frame(pca$x[, 1:4, drop = FALSE]) |>
  rownames_to_column("run") |>
  left_join(sample_info, by = "run") |>
  mutate(
    hover = paste0(
      "Run: ", run, "<br>Sample: ", sample, "<br>Individual: ", individual,
      "<br>Group: ", disease_state, "<br>Timepoint: ", timepoint, "<br>Age: ", age, "<br>Sex: ", sex
    ))
```

### PCA Diagnostics {.tabset}

The first four principal components were examined to assess the major expression patterns in the dataset. Paired baseline and follow-up samples from the same individual are connected to visualise longitudinal movement between timepoints.

#### Variance Explained

This plot shows the proportion of total expression variance explained by the leading principal components. It provides an overview of how strongly the dataset is dominated by the first few dimensions of variation.

```{r pca-variance}
n_pc_shown <- min(10, length(variance_explained))
pca_variance <- tibble(
  PC = factor(paste0("PC", seq_len(n_pc_shown)), levels = paste0("PC", seq_len(n_pc_shown))),
  Variance = variance_explained[seq_len(n_pc_shown)])
plot_ly(
  data = pca_variance, x = ~PC, y = ~Variance, type = "bar",
  text = ~paste0(PC, ": ", round(Variance, 2), "%"), hoverinfo = "text"
) |>
  layout(xaxis = list(title = "Principal component"), yaxis = list(title = "Variance explained (%)")) |>
  format_plotly()
```

#### PC1 vs PC2

PC1 and PC2 represent the two largest directions of variation in the expression matrix. Samples are coloured by disease state and distinguished by timepoint, while paired samples from the same individual are connected by grey lines.

```{r pca-pc1-pc2}
plot_pca_pair <- function(pc_x, pc_y) {
  pc_index <- as.integer(str_remove(c(pc_x, pc_y), "PC"))
  plot_data <- pca_data |>
    mutate(
      x = .data[[pc_x]], y = .data[[pc_y]],
      text = paste0(hover, "<br>", pc_x, ": ", round(x, 2), "<br>", pc_y, ": ", round(y, 2))
    )
  ## Control points are drawn first so that T2D case points sit on top
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x, y)) +
    geom_line(aes(group = individual), color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_point(
      aes(color = disease_state, shape = timepoint, text = text),
      data = dplyr::filter(plot_data, disease_state == "control"), size = 2.5, alpha = 0.85
    ) +
    geom_point(
      aes(color = disease_state, shape = timepoint, text = text),
      data = dplyr::filter(plot_data, disease_state == "T2D case"), size = 2.5, alpha = 0.85
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = disease_colors) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = timepoint_shapes) +
    labs(
      x = paste0(pc_x, " (", round(variance_explained[pc_index[1]], 1), "%)"),
      y = paste0(pc_y, " (", round(variance_explained[pc_index[2]], 1), "%)")
    ) +
    cchc_theme()
  ## Replace the combined (disease state, timepoint) legend with two separate legends
  legend_key <- tibble(
    name = c(names(disease_colors), names(timepoint_shapes)),
    group = rep(c("Disease state", "Timepoint"), c(length(disease_colors), length(timepoint_shapes))),
    color = c(unname(disease_colors), rep("grey40", length(timepoint_shapes))),
    symbol = c(rep("circle", length(disease_colors)), "circle", "circle-open")
  )
  p <- plotly_build(ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text"))
  p$x$data <- lapply(p$x$data, function(tr) modifyList(tr, list(showlegend = FALSE)))
  legend_traces <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(legend_key)), function(i) {
    list(
      type = "scatter", mode = "markers", x = I(NA_real_), y = I(NA_real_), hoverinfo = "skip",
      name = legend_key$name[i], legendgroup = legend_key$group[i],
      legendgrouptitle = list(text = legend_key$group[i]), showlegend = TRUE,
      marker = list(color = legend_key$color[i], symbol = legend_key$symbol[i], size = 9)
    )
  })
  p$x$data <- c(p$x$data, legend_traces)
  p$x$layout$legend <- modifyList(
    p$x$layout$legend,
    list(title = list(text = ""), itemclick = FALSE, itemdoubleclick = FALSE, tracegroupgap = 12)
  )
  format_plotly(p)
}
plot_pca_pair("PC1", "PC2")
```

#### PC3 vs PC4

PC3 and PC4 were also examined because sample-specific or technical variation may not be restricted to the first two principal components. The same disease-state, timepoint, and paired-sample visual encoding is retained for consistency.

```{r pca-pc3-pc4}
plot_pca_pair("PC3", "PC4")
```

# Robust Outlier Detection

Robust outlier detection was applied to PC1-PC4 to identify samples with unusually extreme PCA scores. For each principal component, robust Z-scores were calculated using the median and median absolute deviation (MAD), which are less sensitive to extreme values than the mean and standard deviation.
Two exploratory thresholds were used to classify samples as potential or unambiguous PCA outliers.

```{r robust-outliers}
potential_cutoff <- qnorm(0.995)
unambiguous_cutoff <- qnorm(0.9995)
robust_scores <- pca_data |>
  dplyr::select(run, PC1, PC2, PC3, PC4) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = PC1:PC4, names_to = "PC", values_to = "score") |>
  group_by(PC) |>
  mutate(
    pc_median = median(score, na.rm = TRUE),
    pc_mad = mad(score, na.rm = TRUE),
    robust_z = if_else(pc_mad > 0, (score - pc_median) / pc_mad, NA_real_),
    abs_robust_z = abs(robust_z),
    outlier_status = case_when(
      abs_robust_z >= unambiguous_cutoff ~ "Unambiguous",
      abs_robust_z >= potential_cutoff ~ "Potential",
      TRUE ~ "No"
    )) |>
  ungroup() |>
  left_join(sample_info, by = "run") |>
  mutate(
    hover = paste0(
      "Run: ", run, "<br>Individual: ", individual, "<br>", PC, ": ", round(score, 2),
      "<br>Robust Z: ", round(robust_z, 2), "<br>Status: ", outlier_status))
```

## Robust Z-score Distribution

This plot shows the absolute robust Z-score of each sample across PC1-PC4. Horizontal reference lines indicate the potential and unambiguous outlier thresholds, allowing samples with unusually extreme PCA positions to be identified across multiple principal components.

```{r robust-z-plot}
plot_ly(
  data = robust_scores, x = ~PC, y = ~abs_robust_z, type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
  color = ~outlier_status, colors = outlier_colors,
  text = ~hover, hoverinfo = "text") |>
  layout(
    xaxis = list(title = "Principal component"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Absolute robust Z-score"),
    shapes = list(
      list(
        type = "line", xref = "paper", x0 = 0, x1 = 1, y0 = potential_cutoff, y1 = potential_cutoff,
        line = list(dash = "dash")
      ),
      list(
        type = "line", xref = "paper", x0 = 0, x1 = 1, y0 = unambiguous_cutoff,
        y1 = unambiguous_cutoff, line = list(dash = "dot")
      )
    )) |>
  format_plotly()
```

## Outlier Summary

The outlier summary collapses the PC-specific results to one sample-level classification. Each sample is assigned the most severe status observed across PC1-PC4, and the principal components responsible for the flag are retained for follow-up review.

```{r outlier-summary}
sample_outliers <- robust_scores |>
  group_by(run) |>
  summarise(
    max_abs_robust_z = max(abs_robust_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    flagged_pc = paste(PC[outlier_status != "No"], collapse = ", "),
    sample_outlier_status = case_when(
      any(outlier_status == "Unambiguous") ~ "Unambiguous",
      any(outlier_status == "Potential") ~ "Potential",
      TRUE ~ "No"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(outlier_status = sample_outlier_status) |>
  left_join(sample_info, by = "run") |>
  left_join(
    qc |>
      dplyr::select(
        run, library_size_input_million, library_size_output_million, mapping_rate, library_compatible_pct,
        decoy_pct, fragment_length_mean, rrna_mean_pct, hbrna_mean_pct
      ),
    by = "run"
  )
outlier_counts <- sample_outliers |>
  dplyr::count(outlier_status, name = "Samples")
reactable(outlier_counts, pagination = FALSE, bordered = TRUE, striped = TRUE, highlight = TRUE)
```

# Flagged Sample Review

Samples identified as potential or unambiguous PCA outliers are reviewed in greater detail using available sample metadata and technical QC metrics. The purpose of this step is to investigate whether unusual PCA positions can be explained by known biological or technical characteristics before considering any sample exclusion.

## Flagged Samples

The table below lists all samples flagged in the PCA-based robust outlier analysis together with the principal component responsible for the flag, outlier strength, demographic information, and key technical QC metrics.

```{r flagged-samples}
flagged_samples <- sample_outliers |>
  dplyr::filter(outlier_status != "No") |>
  mutate(
    max_abs_robust_z = round(max_abs_robust_z, 2),
    library_size_input_million = round(library_size_input_million, 2),
    library_size_output_million = round(library_size_output_million, 2),
    mapping_rate = round(mapping_rate, 2),
    library_compatible_pct = round(library_compatible_pct, 2),
    decoy_pct = round(decoy_pct, 2),
    fragment_length_mean = round(fragment_length_mean, 2),
    rrna_mean_pct = round(rrna_mean_pct, 2),
    hbrna_mean_pct = round(hbrna_mean_pct, 2)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(max_abs_robust_z)) |>
  dplyr::select(
    run, individual, disease_state, timepoint, age, sex, outlier_status, flagged_pc, max_abs_robust_z,
    library_size_input_million, library_size_output_million, mapping_rate, library_compatible_pct,
    decoy_pct, fragment_length_mean, rrna_mean_pct, hbrna_mean_pct
  )
reactable(
  flagged_samples,
  searchable = TRUE, sortable = TRUE, resizable = TRUE, filterable = TRUE,
  showPageSizeOptions = TRUE, defaultPageSize = 10, striped = TRUE, highlight = TRUE,
  columns = list(
    run = colDef(name = "Run"),
    individual = colDef(name = "Individual"),
    disease_state = colDef(name = "Disease state"),
    timepoint = colDef(name = "Timepoint"),
    age = colDef(name = "Age"),
    sex = colDef(name = "Sex"),
    outlier_status = colDef(name = "Outlier status"),
    flagged_pc = colDef(name = "Flagged PC"),
    max_abs_robust_z = colDef(name = "Max |robust Z|")
  )
)
```

# Outlier Association

Potential associations between PCA outlier status and available biological or technical variables were examined to identify factors that may contribute to the observed sample structure.

## Biological / Sample Metadata {.tabset}

Available sample-level metadata were examined to determine whether PCA outlier status was associated with demographic characteristics.

### Age by PCA Outlier Status

Age distributions were compared between non-flagged and flagged samples to assess whether PCA outlier status was concentrated within a particular age range.

```{r age-by-outlier-status}
age_outlier_data <- sample_outliers |>
  mutate(
    outlier_binary = if_else(outlier_status == "No", "No", "Flagged"),
    outlier_binary = factor(outlier_binary, levels = c("No", "Flagged")),
    hover = paste0(
      "Run: ", run, "<br>Individual: ", individual, "<br>Age: ", age, "<br>Sex: ", sex,
      "<br>Group: ", disease_state, "<br>Timepoint: ", timepoint,
      "<br>Outlier status: ", outlier_status, "<br>Max |robust Z|: ", round(max_abs_robust_z, 2)
    )
  )
p <- age_outlier_data |>
  ggplot(aes(x = outlier_binary, y = age, color = outlier_binary)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.6, width = 0.55) +
  geom_jitter(aes(text = hover), width = 0.12, height = 0, size = 2.2, alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_color_manual(values = outlier_binary_colors) +
  labs(x = "PCA outlier status", y = "Age (years)", color = "PCA outlier status") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
format_plotly(ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text"))
```

### Sex and PCA Outlier Status

The proportion of flagged samples was summarised by sex to assess whether PCA outliers were disproportionately represented in one sex group.

```{r sex-outlier-summary}
sex_outlier_summary <- sample_outliers |>
  mutate(outlier_binary = if_else(outlier_status == "No", "No", "Flagged")) |>
  group_by(sex) |>
  summarise(
    Samples = n(),
    `Non-flagged` = sum(outlier_binary == "No"),
    Flagged = sum(outlier_binary == "Flagged"),
    `Flagged (%)` = round(mean(outlier_binary == "Flagged") * 100, 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(Sex = sex)
reactable(sex_outlier_summary, pagination = FALSE, bordered = TRUE, striped = TRUE, highlight = TRUE)
```

## Technical QC {.tabset}

Technical QC metrics were compared with PCA outlier status and outlier strength to assess whether unusual expression structure could be related to sequencing depth, mapping behaviour, library characteristics, or whole-blood RNA composition.

```{r qc-association-data}
qc_metric_labels <- c(
  library_size_input_million = "Input library size (million fragments)",
  library_size_output_million = "Output library size (million mapped fragments)",
  mapping_rate = "Mapping rate (%)",
  library_compatible_pct = "Library compatibility (%)",
  decoy_pct = "Decoy fragments (%)",
  fragment_length_mean = "Mean fragment length (bp)",
  rrna_mean_pct = "rRNA (%)",
  hbrna_mean_pct = "HbRNA (%)"
)
qc_association <- sample_outliers |>
  mutate(
    outlier_binary = if_else(outlier_status == "No", "No", "Flagged"),
    outlier_binary = factor(outlier_binary, levels = c("No", "Flagged"))
  )
qc_association_long <- qc_association |>
  dplyr::select(
    run, individual, disease_state, timepoint, outlier_status, outlier_binary, max_abs_robust_z,
    all_of(names(qc_metric_labels))
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(names(qc_metric_labels)), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(
    metric_label = factor(metric, levels = names(qc_metric_labels), labels = unname(qc_metric_labels)),
    hover = paste0(
      "Run: ", run, "<br>Individual: ", individual, "<br>Group: ", disease_state, "<br>Timepoint: ", timepoint,
      "<br>Outlier status: ", outlier_status, "<br>QC value: ", round(value, 2),
      "<br>Max |robust Z|: ", round(max_abs_robust_z, 2)
    ))
```

### QC Metrics by Outlier Status

QC metric distributions were compared between non-flagged and flagged samples. This provides a direct view of whether flagged samples tend to have systematically different technical characteristics from the remainder of the cohort.

```{r qc-association-boxplots}
p <- qc_association_long |>
  ggplot(aes(x = outlier_binary, y = value, color = outlier_binary)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_jitter(aes(text = hover), width = 0.15, height = 0, size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric_label, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = outlier_binary_colors) +
  labs(x = "PCA outlier status", y = NULL, color = "PCA outlier status")
format_plotly(ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text"))
```

### QC Metrics vs PCA Outlier Strength

Each QC metric was also compared with the maximum absolute robust Z-score to assess whether increasingly extreme PCA positions were associated with increasingly unusual technical measurements.

```{r qc-vs-robust-z}
p <- qc_association_long |>
  ggplot(aes(x = value, y = max_abs_robust_z)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = outlier_status, shape = outlier_status, text = hover), size = 2.3, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = potential_cutoff, linetype = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = unambiguous_cutoff, linetype = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric_label, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = outlier_colors) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = outlier_shapes) +
  labs(x = "QC metric value", y = "Maximum absolute robust Z-score", color = "Outlier status", shape = "Outlier status")
format_plotly(ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text"))
```

### QC Association Summary

The summary table quantifies the exploratory relationships shown above. Median QC values are reported for non-flagged and flagged samples.

```{r qc-association-summary}
qc_association_summary <- qc_association_long |>
  group_by(metric, metric_label) |>
  summarise(
    non_flagged_n = sum(outlier_binary == "No" & !is.na(value)),
    flagged_n = sum(outlier_binary == "Flagged" & !is.na(value)),
    non_flagged_median = median(value[outlier_binary == "No"], na.rm = TRUE),
    flagged_median = median(value[outlier_binary == "Flagged"], na.rm = TRUE),
    spearman_rho = suppressWarnings(cor(value, max_abs_robust_z, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")),
    wilcoxon_p = tryCatch(wilcox.test(value ~ outlier_binary, exact = FALSE)$p.value, error = function(e) NA_real_),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(FDR = p.adjust(wilcoxon_p, method = "BH")) |>
  arrange(FDR, desc(abs(spearman_rho))) |>
  transmute(
    Metric = as.character(metric_label),
    `Non-flagged n` = non_flagged_n,
    `Flagged n` = flagged_n,
    `Non-flagged median` = round(non_flagged_median, 2),
    `Flagged median` = round(flagged_median, 2),
    `Spearman rho` = round(spearman_rho, 3),
    `Wilcoxon p` = signif(wilcoxon_p, 3),
    FDR = signif(FDR, 3)
  )
reactable(
  qc_association_summary,
  pagination = FALSE, bordered = TRUE, striped = TRUE, highlight = TRUE,
  columns = list(
    Metric = colDef(name = "QC metric"),
    `Spearman rho` = colDef(name = "Spearman rho"),
    `Wilcoxon p` = colDef(name = "Wilcoxon p"),
    FDR = colDef(name = "BH-adjusted p")
  ))
```

# Unwanted Variation Assessment

Unwanted variation was assessed using RUVg to determine whether latent technical or sample-level factors could explain part of the expression structure observed during PCA.

## RUV Setup

The same samples and gene filter used in the preceding expression-level assessment were retained for the RUV analysis.

```{r ruv-setup}
# Length-scaled gene-level counts
txi_ruv <- tximport(
  quant_files, type = "salmon", tx2gene = tx2gene, ignoreTxVersion = TRUE, dropInfReps = TRUE,
  countsFromAbundance = "lengthScaledTPM"
)
# Confirm that gene ordering is identical to the original tximport object
stopifnot(identical(rownames(txi_ruv$counts), rownames(gene_counts)))
# Keep the same gene set used in the preceding expression-level assessment
ruv_counts <- txi_ruv$counts[keep, , drop = FALSE]
ruv_pheno <- as.data.frame(sample_info)
rownames(ruv_pheno) <- ruv_pheno$run
stopifnot(identical(colnames(ruv_counts), rownames(ruv_pheno)))
ruv_pheno$individual <- factor(ruv_pheno$individual)
ruv_pheno$timepoint <- relevel(factor(ruv_pheno$timepoint), ref = "baseline")
ruv_pheno$disease_state <- relevel(factor(ruv_pheno$disease_state), ref = "control")
ruv_pheno$case_followup <- as.integer(ruv_pheno$disease_state == "T2D case" & ruv_pheno$timepoint == "follow-up")
ruv_sample_colors <- timepoint_colors[as.character(ruv_pheno$timepoint)]
```

## RLE Before TMM Normalization

Relative log expression (RLE) distributions were examined before between-library normalisation to assess sample-level shifts in global expression.

```{r ruv-rle-before}
plotRLE(ruv_counts, outline = FALSE, ylim = c(-4, 4), col = ruv_sample_colors)
```

## PCA Before TMM Normalization

PCA was examined before TMM normalisation to provide a reference view of the major sample-level expression structure before between-library scaling was applied.

```{r ruv-pca-before}
plotPCA(ruv_counts, col = ruv_sample_colors, cex = 1.2)
```

## TMM Normalization

TMM (Trimmed Mean of M-values) normalisation was applied to account for between-library differences in sequencing depth and RNA composition.

```{r ruv-tmm}
ruv_y <- DGEList(counts = ruv_counts)
ruv_y <- normLibSizes(ruv_y, method = "TMM")
ruv_tmm_cpm <- cpm(ruv_y, log = FALSE, normalized.lib.sizes = TRUE)
ruv_tmm_logcpm <- cpm(ruv_y, log = TRUE, prior.count = 1, normalized.lib.sizes = TRUE)
```

## RLE After TMM Normalization

RLE distributions were re-examined after TMM normalisation to assess whether between-library scaling reduced sample-level shifts in global expression.

```{r ruv-rle-after-tmm}
plotRLE(ruv_tmm_cpm, outline = FALSE, ylim = c(-4, 4), col = ruv_sample_colors)
```

## PCA After TMM Normalization

PCA was reassessed after TMM normalisation to determine which major expression patterns remained after between-library scaling.

```{r ruv-pca-after-tmm}
plotPCA(ruv_tmm_logcpm, isLog = TRUE, col = ruv_sample_colors, cex = 1.2)
```

## First-pass edgeR Analysis

A first-pass edgeR analysis was performed to rank genes for empirical negative-control selection. The model accounts for individual identity and longitudinal structure so that genes showing the strongest evidence of timepoint- or case-associated change can be separated from genes used to estimate unwanted variation.

```{r ruv-empirical-control-ranking}
control_design <- model.matrix(~ individual + timepoint + case_followup, data = ruv_pheno)
control_fit <- glmQLFit(ruv_y, design = control_design, legacy = FALSE)
control_test_coef <- grep("^(timepoint|case_followup)", colnames(control_design))
stopifnot(length(control_test_coef) == 2)
control_test <- glmQLFTest(control_fit, coef = control_test_coef)
control_ranking <- topTags(control_test, n = Inf, sort.by = "PValue")$table |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  rownames_to_column("gene_id")
```

## Empirical Control Genes

Two empirical control-gene definitions were evaluated to assess the sensitivity of RUVg to control selection.
The first follows the RUVSeq example by excluding the 5,000 most significant genes from the first-pass ranking and using all remaining genes as empirical controls. The second uses the least significant 50% of ranked genes as a more conservative control set.

```{r ruv-empirical-controls}
# Strategy 1: exclude the 5,000 most significant genes
top5000_genes <- control_ranking |>
  slice_head(n = min(5000, nrow(control_ranking))) |>
  pull(gene_id)
empirical_controls_exclude5000 <- setdiff(rownames(ruv_counts), top5000_genes)
# Strategy 2: use the least significant 50% of ranked genes
empirical_controls_bottom50 <- control_ranking |>
  slice_tail(n = floor(nrow(control_ranking) * 0.5)) |>
  pull(gene_id) |>
  intersect(rownames(ruv_counts))
control_sets <- list(exclude_top5000 = empirical_controls_exclude5000, bottom50 = empirical_controls_bottom50)
control_labels <- c(exclude_top5000 = "Exclude top 5000", bottom50 = "Bottom 50%")
tibble(
  `Control strategy` = unname(control_labels[names(control_sets)]),
  `Genes ranked` = nrow(control_ranking),
  `Control genes` = lengths(control_sets)
) |>
  reactable(pagination = FALSE, bordered = TRUE, striped = TRUE, highlight = TRUE)
```

## RUVg Across k = 1 to 10

RUVg was evaluated across `k = 1-10` for both empirical control-gene definitions. All other analysis settings were held constant so that differences between the resulting PCA structures reflect sensitivity to control-gene selection.
For each control strategy, increasing values of `k` estimate increasing numbers of latent unwanted factors. The aim is to assess whether the overall RUVg sensitivity pattern is consistent across alternative empirical control definitions.

```{r ruvg-fits}
ruv_k_values <- 1:10
ruv_fits <- purrr::map(control_sets, function(controls) {
  purrr::map(ruv_k_values, function(k) RUVg(ruv_tmm_logcpm, controls, k = k, isLog = TRUE, round = FALSE)) |>
    setNames(paste0("k", ruv_k_values))
})
```

## PCA Across Empirical Control Strategies

PCA was recalculated for each combination of empirical control-gene strategy and `k`.

```{r ruvg-pca-data}
ruv_pca_data <- purrr::imap_dfr(ruv_fits, function(control_fits, control_id) {
  purrr::map_dfr(ruv_k_values, function(k) {
    pca_k <- prcomp(t(control_fits[[paste0("k", k)]]$normalizedCounts), center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)
    variance_k <- (pca_k$sdev^2 / sum(pca_k$sdev^2)) * 100
    as.data.frame(pca_k$x[, 1:2, drop = FALSE]) |>
      rownames_to_column("run") |>
      mutate(
        control_id = control_id, control_method = unname(control_labels[control_id]), k = k,
        pc1_variance = variance_k[1], pc2_variance = variance_k[2]
      )
  })
}) |>
  left_join(sample_info, by = "run") |>
  mutate(
    disease_state = factor(disease_state, levels = c("control", "T2D case")),
    timepoint = factor(timepoint, levels = c("baseline", "follow-up"))
  )
```

```{r ruvg-pca-function}
## Fixed axis limits shared by every strategy and k, centred on zero
ruv_pc1_lim <- c(-1, 1) * max(abs(ruv_pca_data$PC1))
ruv_pc2_lim <- c(-1, 1) * max(abs(ruv_pca_data$PC2))
plot_ruv_pca_tabs <- function(control_id_selected) {
  for (k_value in ruv_k_values) {
    ruv_pca_k <- ruv_pca_data |>
      dplyr::filter(control_id == control_id_selected, k == k_value)
    cat("\n\n#### k = ", k_value, "\n\n", sep = "")
    p <- ggplot(ruv_pca_k, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = disease_state, shape = timepoint)) +
      stat_ellipse(
        aes(group = interaction(disease_state, timepoint), color = disease_state, linetype = timepoint),
        level = 0.95, linewidth = 0.8
      ) +
      geom_point(size = 2.8, alpha = 0.85) +
      scale_color_manual(values = disease_colors) +
      scale_shape_manual(values = c("baseline" = 19, "follow-up" = 21)) +
      scale_linetype_manual(values = c("baseline" = "solid", "follow-up" = "dashed")) +
      labs(
        x = paste0("PC1 (", round(ruv_pca_k$pc1_variance[1], 1), "%)"),
        y = paste0("PC2 (", round(ruv_pca_k$pc2_variance[1], 1), "%)"),
        color = "Disease state", shape = "Timepoint", linetype = "Timepoint"
      ) +
      coord_cartesian(xlim = ruv_pc1_lim, ylim = ruv_pc2_lim) +
      cchc_theme()
    print(p)
  }
}
```

### Exclude Top 5000 {.tabset}

This strategy excludes the 5,000 genes with the strongest evidence of longitudinal or case-associated expression change in the first-pass edgeR analysis and uses the remaining genes as empirical controls.

```{r ruvg-pca-exclude-top5000, results = "asis", fig.width = 9, fig.height = 7}
plot_ruv_pca_tabs("exclude_top5000")
```

### Bottom 50% {.tabset}

This strategy uses the least significant 50% of genes from the first-pass edgeR ranking as empirical controls.

```{r ruvg-pca-bottom50, results = "asis", fig.width = 9, fig.height = 7}
plot_ruv_pca_tabs("bottom50")
```
